material.mattext: Which of the following is NOT a measure of central tendency?
Mode
Median
Range
Mean
The measure of central tendency that is nost influenced by extreme values is the:
Mode
Median
Range
Mean
Measures of variablity, such as the range and standard deviation, provide information about:
How data is distributed
The most common value in the dataset
The average value of the data
The shape of the data distribution
Which of the following statements best describes the concept of positive feedback?
It maintains stability in a system by countering changes.
It amplifies changes in a system, leading to further change in the same direction.
It has no impact on the system
It leads to a gradual decrease in the system's output.
Selection bias in research refers to:
The tendency for participants to alter their behavior when they know they are being observed.
A systematic error that occurs when the sample of participants is not representative of the population being studied.
The influence of researcher expectations on participants' responses.
The distortion of data in an experiment.
What does the 50th percentile represent in a dataset?
The highest value
The lowest value
The middle value
The range of values

In a study measuring reaction times of 100 participants, the following reaction times (in milliseconds) were recorded: 120, 130, 140, 150, 160, 170, 180, 190, 200, 210, 220, 230, 240, 250, 260, 270, 280, 290, 300, 310, 320, 330, 340, 350, 360, 370, 380, 390, 400, 410, 420, 430, 440, 450, 460, 470, 480, 490, 500, 510, 520, 530, 540, 550, 560, 570, 580, 590, 600.

Calculate the 75th percentile of the reaction times. (2 marks)
440 milliseconds
480 milliseconds
490 milliseconds
550 milliseconds

In a psychological study measuring anxiety levels in a group of 20 participants, the following anxiety scores were recorded: 12, 15, 18, 22, 24, 25, 28, 30, 32, 35, 38, 40, 42, 44, 45, 47, 50, 52, 55, and 58.

Calculate the standard deviation of the anxiety scores. (2 marks)
Reliability in research refers to:
The consistency of measurement or results over time
The accuracy of the research findings
The generalizability of the results to different populations
The extent to which the research is free from biases
Validity in research refers to:
The consistency of measurement or results over time
The accuracy of the research findings
The generalizability of the results to different populations.
The extent to which the research is free from biases
Which of the following scenarios is an example of selection bias in a research study?
Participants in a drug trial are assigned to treatment or placebo groups based on a random lottery.
A researcher selects only participants from a specific age group, excluding other age groups.
Researchers use double-blind procedures to eliminate bias in their study.
Participants are given a placebo, leading to the placebo effect.
Positive feedback in a feedback loop:
Maintains stability in a system
Amplifies a change in the system
Counteracts change in the system
no effect on the system
Which of the following is an example of a double-blind experiment?
The researcher knows which participants are in the control group, but the participants do not.
Both the researcher and the participants are unaware of who is in the experimental and control groups.
The researcher knows which participants are in the experimental group, but the participants do not.
The researcher and participants are aware of group assignments.
The Hawthorne Effect refers to:
A type of statistical illusion
The tendency for participants to behave differently when they know they are being observed
The reinterpretation of research results to fit a particular hypothesis
The placebo effect in research
How can researchers mitigate selection bias in experimental psychology studies?
By randomly assigning participants to groups or conditions.
By providing participants with detailed feedback about their performance.
By using positive feedback mechanisms to encourage participation.
By conducting observational studies rather than experiments.
The Hawthorne Effect is related to the potential presence of selection bias because:
It can result in participants altering their behavior due to the awareness of being observed.
It is a type of statistical illusion.
It occurs when participants are not randomly assigned to groups.
It is caused by a lack of blinding in the research design.
Inattentional blindness refers to:
The tendency to misinterpret research findings
Failing to notice a visible object or event because one's attention is focused elsewhere
The bias in selecting participants for a study
The distortion of data in an experiment
Statistical illusions in research may arise from:
Accurate data analysis
Appropriate research design
Misleading data presentation or interpretation
Random sampling
The placebo effect is an example of:
A double-blind experiment
A positive feedback loop
A statistical illusion
The impact of expectations on behaviour or perception
The reinterpretation effect in research refers to:
The tendency to notice unexpected objects or events while focusing on a primary task
A statistical illusion resulting from random sampling errors
The distortion of research findings to fit a predetermined hypothesis
The placebo effect on participants' perception
Which of the following research scenarios is an example of positive feedback?
Participants reporting decreased pain perception after receiving a placebo
A researcher continually adjusting the experimental conditions to maintain consistent results
An amplification of participants' response to a new stimulus
Researchers consistently finding no effect in their experiments
Webster is hungry so he decides to eat an apple to reduce his hunger.  This is an example of _____ feedback.
Positive
Negative
fluctuating
neutral
Which one of the following terms is NOT a category of reliability?
External
Internal
Test-retest
Inter-rater
